model.description: The machine the printer says it is, such as MK4S, which a page draws its picture for. Absent for a printer that said nothing.

state.description: The printer's own word for what it is doing, such as IDLE, READY, PRINTING or FINISHED.

connected.description: False for a printer that is away.

can_be_ready.description: The printer takes the command that marks it as ready.

free.description: The printer takes a print now.

ready.description: A person told the printer its bed is clear.

paused.description: The printer has a print paused: it takes the command that resumes one.

storage.description: The storage the file is in, and empty for a file already on the printer.

path.description: The file inside that storage, or its path on the printer, such as usb/bracket.bgcode.

name.description: The file's name without its folders.

added_by.description: The principal of the person who put the file on the queue.

note.description: Why a waiting file did not start. After send_failed, transfer_failed, not_started and taken_back the file waits for a person to start it. not_arrived is a file added while it was copied to the printer that is not there yet. taken_back is a file a person stopped on its way to the printer.

detail.description: The server's or the printer's own words for the note.

started_by.description: Who started the print, and empty for the queue itself.

landing.description: Where the file was written on the printer.

attempts.description: How often the file was sent.

arriving.description: True for a file on the printer that was added while it was copied there and that nothing has seen on the printer yet.

estimated_seconds.description: How long the slicer said the file prints, in whole seconds, read when the file was added. Absent for a file that does not say, and for one nobody could ask about.

printer_model.description: The printer the file was sliced for, such as XL2IS, read when the file was added. Absent for a file that does not say.

layer_height_mm.description: The layer height the file was sliced with, in millimetres. Absent for a file that does not say.

material.description: The material the file was sliced for, one for each tool joined by a semicolon, such as PLA;PETG. Absent for a file that does not say.

size.description: The file's size in bytes, read when the file was added. Absent when nobody could ask.

modified.description: When a file on the printer was last written, in seconds since the Unix epoch. With the size it names the version of the file. Absent for a file in a storage, and when nobody could ask.

job_id.description: The server's id of the print, once the printer opened it.

max_waiting.description: How many files may wait on one printer.

keep_history.description: How many ended prints a queue keeps.

entries.description: The file on its way or printing first, if there is one, and then the waiting files in the order they print.

starts_alone.description: The queue may start the next file by itself once the printer is ready. Without it a person starts each file. The answer with every queue says it only for a queue with a file waiting, and false for the others.

may_change.description: The caller may print on the printer, so may change its queue.

remaining_seconds.description: How long the printer says the print from the queue still takes, in seconds. Absent when nothing from the queue prints, and when the printer does not say.

progress.description: How far the printer says the print from the queue is, in whole percent. Absent when nothing from the queue prints, and when the printer does not say.

storage.description: The storage the file is in, by the name it is declared under. Leave it out for a file already on the printer.

path.description: The file inside that storage, or the file's path on the printer, such as usb/bracket.bgcode.

position.description: Where the file goes among the waiting files, 0 being the next one. Absent is the end.

arriving.description: The file is being copied to path on the printer right now, so it is added without looking for it there. It goes with no storage. The queue looks for the file when its turn comes, and an entry whose file is not there waits with the note not_arrived.

position.description: The new position among the waiting files, 0 being the next one.

ready.description: True says the bed is clear. False takes that back.

info.title: simple-queue
info.description: The routes the simple-queue module serves. Every path is relative to the mount the host assigns, and the host serves this document rebased under it at <mount>/openapi.json.

get.description: The files of one printer's queue in the order they print, the ended prints, the printer's state, and whether the caller may change the queue. A printer with no queue answers an empty one. The host takes view_resource on the module's instance before this is called, which a credential with the read scope reaches. The module then asks the server whether the caller may see the printer.

post.summary: Put a file on the queue
post.description: Puts a print file at the end of the queue, or at the position the body names. The file is in one of this server's storages, which takes read_storage, or already on the printer when the body names no storage. It must be a print file. When the printer is ready and prints nothing from the queue, the file starts at once, as the caller. The host takes operate_resource on the module's instance before this is called, which a credential with the operate scope reaches. The module then asks the server whether the caller may print on the printer.
